title: The Hidden Cost of Interruptions Isn't Time

sources.citation: Mark, Gudith & Klocke (2008). The Cost of Interrupted Work: More Speed and Stress. CHI 2008.
claims_used: interrupted tasks completed in LESS time, no quality difference
after 20 min of interrupted work: significantly higher stress, frustration, workload, effort, pressure

segments.text: Everyone tells you interruptions waste your time. The research says the opposite. And what they actually cost you is far more dangerous.
In a controlled study at the University of California, Gloria Mark found that interrupted workers finished their tasks in less time, with no drop in quality. They simply worked faster to compensate.

But that speed has a hidden price. After just twenty minutes of interrupted work, people reported significantly higher stress, frustration, and mental effort. You don't lose the minutes. You burn the fuel.
So stop measuring focus by the clock. Protect your attention not to save time, but to protect the energy you need to do the work that matters.
